Control_Objective: A qualified operator can monitor, interpret, intervene in, override and halt the system throughout its operation, supported by documented procedures and interfaces.
Oversight roles, responsibilities and competences are formally assigned, documented and communicated.
The system can be halted or control transferred to a human, and that mechanism functions under fault conditions.
Oversight actions - interventions, overrides and halts - are recorded in tamper-evident logs reviewable by authorised personnel.
Notes: Grounding provisional pending publication of the logging standard.

Control_Objective: Perturbation types, magnitudes and acceptance thresholds relevant to the intended use are documented and justified before testing, and measured performance degradation stays within them.
Notes: Paired: thresholds must be documented before the test is run.

Control_Objective: Distributional shift in operational inputs and outputs is detected against documented metrics and thresholds, and threshold breaches trigger the documented escalation.
The AI product is covered by an information security management system with documented risk assessment, controls and treatment.
Notes: GAP: organisational control only. Art. 15(5) names data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples and confidentiality attacks; no AI-specific security test is specified. Consider adding adversarial testing as a local extension.

Control_Objective: A documented incident-handling process covers detection, response, recovery and lessons learned.
Model confidence scores are calibrated against a documented method and acceptance criteria, evidenced on a held-out set representative of operational conditions.
Fail-safe modes, triggering conditions and transition latencies are documented, and the system transitions to the documented safe state within the specified latency under injected faults.
Training, validation and testing datasets meet documented criteria for accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness and representativeness.
Documented procedures govern data collection, labelling, cleaning and access management, and are demonstrably followed.
Where personal data is processed, a documented lawful basis exists and processing is confined to the specified purpose.
Pseudonymisation, minimisation and access controls are implemented from the design stage, and only authorised roles access personal data in operation.
Notes: Paired: control tests existence of design measures, test verifies operational effectiveness.

Control_Objective: Personal data is encrypted at rest and in transit, with access controls and logging demonstrably effective.
Dataset versions, transformations and lineage are tracked such that any dataset state used in training, validation or testing can be reproduced.
Instructions for use document the intended purpose, capabilities, limitations, performance characteristics and required human oversight.
Structured documentation covers training data, methods, performance metrics and known limitations.
Standards_Grounding: ISO/IEC 42001 Sec. 7.5, Ann. A.6.2; ISO/IEC 23894 Sec. 6.3

Control_Objective: The system produces output-level explanations consistent with documented explainability techniques.
Where Article 50 applies, persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system or that content is AI-generated.
Notes: CONDITIONAL: applies only to direct interaction with natural persons, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, deepfakes and AI-generated public-interest text. Not applicable to all high-risk systems by default.

Control_Objective: Datasets are analysed for representational and measurement bias, with protected attributes or relevant subgroups, metrics and findings documented.
Notes: TR 24027 is informative: no prescribed metrics or thresholds.

Control_Objective: Model performance is disaggregated by relevant subgroups using documented fairness metrics, and subgroups falling below documented thresholds are flagged.
Notes: Metric selection is left to the provider. Procedural accountability only: an assessor can verify the choice was documented and justified, not that it was adequate.

Control_Objective: Documented procedures address identified biases at data, model and post-deployment level, with mitigation actions traced to specific findings from R5.1 and R5.2.
Standards_Grounding: ISO/IEC 42001 Ann. A.6.2, A.7; ISO/IEC TR 24027

Control_Objective: Where the provider has committed to addressing societal and environmental impacts, those impacts are documented within the AI management system.
Notes: VOLUNTARY: no dedicated operative article. Art. 9(2)(a) limits risk management to health, safety and fundamental rights; environmental risk is not enumerated. Exclude from a mandatory register or tag as non-binding.

Control_Objective: Where committed, computational resource consumption associated with the AI product is monitored.
Notes: VOLUNTARY: grounded in Art. 95 codes of conduct only.

Control_Objective: Roles, responsibilities and authorities for AI activities are documented and communicated.
Standards_Grounding: ISO/IEC 42001 Sec. 5.3, Ann. A.4; ISO 9001 Sec. 5.3

Control_Objective: Retained, tamper-evident logs are sufficient to reconstruct relevant system operations.
Controlled, versioned documentation enables an audit to reconstruct compliance evidence.
A documented AI quality policy with measurable objectives is approved by top management.
Notes: prEN 18286 is the future Tier 1 instrument for Art. 17; at public enquiry stage.

Control_Objective: QMS documentation is controlled and versioned across all lifecycle activities.
Internal audits are planned, executed and recorded, with non-conformities tracked through to closure.
Management reviews are conducted, documented, and drive improvement actions.
The intended purpose, scope and context of use are documented as the basis for risk management.

Risks to health, safety and fundamental rights are systematically identified across the lifecycle - data, model, integration and deployment - and the Art. 6 / Annex III classification step is documented.
Standards_Grounding: ISO/IEC 23894 Sec. 6.4; ISO 31000; ISO/IEC 31010; ISO/IEC TR 24027
Notes: Risk scope is fixed by Art. 9(2)(a) and does not extend to environmental risk.

Control_Objective: Identified risks are analysed for likelihood and severity and evaluated against documented acceptance criteria.
Risk treatment measures are documented, implemented and traced to the risks they address.
Residual risks are evaluated against acceptance criteria and formally accepted by an authorised role.
A documented post-market monitoring plan defines monitoring, logging and reporting activities.
Monitoring data is collected, retained and analysed in accordance with the post-market monitoring plan.
Non-conformities and incidents trigger documented corrective and preventive actions.
Standards_Grounding: ISO/IEC 42001 Sec. 10; ISO 9001 Sec. 10; ISO/IEC 23894 Sec. 6.6

Control_Objective: Procedures exist to detect, document and report serious incidents in line with Art. 73 deadlines.
Technical documentation covers the intended purpose, deployment context and overall system description.
Architecture, design choices and component integration are documented with traceability to risks and requirements.
Dataset provenance, quality attributes and limitations are documented.
Standards_Grounding: ISO/IEC 42001 Sec. 7.5, 8.3; ISO/IEC 5259-2; ISO/IEC 5259-4; ISO/IEC TR 24027

Control_Objective: Performance, robustness and validation results are documented with traceable methods and test conditions.
Documentation includes a structured mapping showing how each essential requirement is satisfied.
The system automatically generates logs covering events relevant to traceability and post-market monitoring over its lifetime.
Versions of data, models and components are recorded to enable reproducibility.
Lineage links connect raw data, processed datasets, trained models and deployed artefacts.

Retention and deletion policies are defined and implemented: technical documentation, QMS records and conformity assessment documentation retained 10 years after placing on the market (Art. 18); automatically generated logs retained by the provider (Art. 19); personal data subject to GDPR storage limitation.
